perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s perspective:

- I am Keith Ndiaye, a construction worker; I am African American, have a bachelor’s degree, and have an ISFJ personality. I work with Elizabeth Sun, the receptionist at our construction company; we have a friendly but professional relationship and often interact during my office visits for paperwork/project updates.
- I noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt/short with me over the past few days. I wondered if I had unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- I asked her if I had done something to upset her. She said no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- I felt sympathetic. I told her I understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. She accepted and thanked me.
- During the coffee break, she shared more about her stresses, which seemed quite severe to me. I thanked her for sharing and asked if she had considered talking to a professional, saying an outside perspective can help. She said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant.
- Afterward, I noticed she became slightly withdrawn. I worried I might have embarrassed her or overstepped.
- I told her I hoped I hadn’t overstepped and that I’m here to support her. She said I didn’t overstep, appreciated my concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, she seemed more open and appreciative. I believed she valued my support and felt more comfortable around me. I told her I was glad we talked and that I’m always available to chat or take a break. She thanked me, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had my support.
- I intend to maintain this supportive relationship.
- I do not know Elizabeth’s private thoughts or facts she did not tell me.
